About the Team 
 Activations is part of StackAdapt's Data Hub product, our customer data platform. Advertisers bring their first-party data into Data Hub: CRM lists, website and app events, product catalogs and store locations. Activations turn that data into something they can use. We build audiences, keep them in sync with the channels advertisers buy on, and feed products and locations into dynamic creative.
 We are a small team of senior and mid-level engineers. We work mostly in Go, on event-driven services that run at large scale, using Kafka, gRPC and TiDB on AWS. Advertisers spend against the audiences we build, and privacy law shapes how we handle their data, so correctness matters as much as speed.
 The team runs flat. Senior engineers lead projects from design to launch. You will set the technical standard those project leads work to: how we design, review and ship. You will help every engineer on the team get better at it, mostly by building alongside them.
 You will work closely with our Data Hub architect, who sets technical direction across the whole domain and decides designs that cross Data Hub teams. You decide designs inside Activations, and the two of you work together on the ones that cross the line. You also own the technical calls the team makes day to day, and the case for changing direction when what we learn in production says we should.
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Owning the technical health of the team's systems. You will own audience evaluation, CRM and programmatic audience syncs, and the product and location feeds behind dynamic creative. You will decide where reliability, cost and tech debt work goes, and make the case for it on the roadmap.
 Building. You will write production code every week and take on the hardest work yourself: how we evaluate audiences at scale, how we keep long-running syncs reliable, and how activation grows beyond email to new identifiers.
 Setting the review bar. A growing share of our code is written with AI coding agents. You will define what a good review looks like when an agent wrote the first draft, review the risky changes yourself, and teach the team to catch what agents miss: concurrency, data correctness, idempotency, privacy.
 Coaching engineers. You will help senior engineers lead their own projects, and help mid-level engineers grow into senior ones. Expect to do this through design reviews, pairing and code reviews that teach.
 Making the team faster with AI, carefully. You will find where AI tools save real time for us, such as review assistants, test generation, runbooks and on-call triage. You will build or adopt those tools, measure whether they work, and drop the ones that don't.
 Turning product needs into technical plans. You will work with Product and the engineering teams around us to shape multi-month plans. You will find unknowns and cross-team dependencies early, and explain trade-offs in plain language.
 Leading on reliability. You will take part in the on-call rotation, lead root cause analysis for team incidents, and make sure the fixes hold. You will set the team's standards for testing, observability and alerting.
 What You'll Bring to the Table 
 8+ years building backend systems, with several years as the engineer others turned to for design decisions on a team that owns production services.
 Strong Go, or deep experience in another backend language and a willingness to work in Go every day.
 Experience designing and running distributed, data-heavy systems: event streaming (Kafka or similar), workflow orchestration, high-volume batch or streaming pipelines, and SQL/NewSQL stores at scale.
 Has led a multi-month project across teams, from design to production.
 Has led incident response and root cause analysis for production services.
 A track record of raising a team's engineering standards beyond code review, through artifacts others adopted: design docs, review guidelines, shared libraries, CI checks, runbooks.
 Real experience with AI coding tools: you use them to build, you know where they fail, and you have helped others use them well. 
 Evidence that engineers grew because of you, through mentoring, sponsorship, or by stepping back so someone else could lead.
 Clear writing. Most of our decisions are made in design docs and pull requests.
 Good judgment about trade-offs: when to ship the simple thing, when to pay down debt, and when to push back.
 Bonus: Ad tech, marketing technology or customer data platforms (identity resolution, audience segmentation, CRM integrations).
 Bonus: Privacy and data deletion compliance (CCPA/CPRA, data broker deletion requests, GDPR).
 Bonus: Temporal, gRPC/protobuf, TiDB or Vitess.

Role Overview

Owner is the leading all-in-one platform for independent restaurants. Guest App Platform is the distribution machine behind thousands of white-labeled restaurant apps: it launches them, signs them, and keeps every one current on the App Store and Google Play at minimal cost.

We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be the technical lead for that platform as we scale to more and more restaurants. You'll work on problems that look very different from a typical mobile role: Temporal workflows that run across thousands of apps, CI/CD and build infrastructure, code signing and provisioning across Apple and Google accounts at scale, and automation (including AI) that removes manual steps while keeping a human fallback where it matters.

This is a high-ownership, hands-on role. You'll be the technical anchor for the Guest App Platform team, setting strategy, keeping the team focused on its goals, and making the platform self-serve so product teams and Launch Specialists can ship into the app without us.

This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada. For San Francisco-based candidates: we have a new HQ in the Presidio for optional in-person collaboration.

Why we’re looking for you

The Guest App Platform team is responsible for launching and keeping thousands of white-labeled apps up to date while keeping costs at a minimum. We don't build guest-facing features. We build the distribution machine underneath every app, and the tooling that lets product teams and our Launch Specialists ship into it. If a restaurant joins Owner, our platform is how their app reaches the App Store and stays healthy.

This is not a normal mobile role. Most mobile engineers keep a handful of apps up to date. We manage thousands, day in and day out, across Apple and Google ecosystems, and we automate everything we can, including with AI.

Our Tech Stack

 - Mobile: React Native, Typescript, iOS and Android (universal binaries re-skinned and re-signed per brand)

 - Orchestration: Temporal, scheduled workers, Human-in-the-loop systems

 - Infrastructure & Tooling: CI/CD pipelines, IP proxies, Kubernetes, in-house bulk deployment tooling

 - Backend & Internal Tools: Node.js, TypeScript, Postgresql, Kubernetes, various AWS services.

 - Automation & AI: Browser automation, AI-assisted workflows

 - Lead the team technically: set strategy and priorities, make architecture decisions, and keep the team focused on its goals

 - Operate apps at fleet scale: own how thousands of separately branded apps are built, signed, deployed and kept current. Design reliable, observable workflows for launches, releases, store submissions and account operations

 - Own CI/CD and build infrastructure: make builds faster, cheaper and more reliable for other developers.

 - Build the tooling our internal customers need: full-stack tools for Launch Specialists and product teams so they can launch and maintain apps without minimal intervention for us.

 - Delete manual steps: find the work humans do repeatedly and automate it, using AI where it makes sense and keeping humans in the loop where it doesn't

 - Navigate Apple and Google: certificates, provisioning, agreements, App Store review and compliance, at scale

 - Partner across the company: work with product engineering, Launch Specialists and leadership, technical and non-technical alike

 - Build the team: mentor engineers, interview candidates and raise the bar

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Core Infrastructure team builds the software systems that power engineering workflows across Cerebras.

Our infrastructure coordinates complex work across machines, clusters, development environments, and hardware systems. We build orchestration frameworks, execution engines, scheduling systems, test infrastructure, developer tools, and reusable software platforms that allow engineers to build, test, qualify, and deliver software reliably at scale.

These systems are primarily built in Python, but the work goes far beyond scripting or automation. Our frameworks act as the control plane for distributed workflows, managing resources, execution state, concurrency, failures, retries, dependencies, and observability across large and complex environments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring a Software Engineer to design and build the core software behind Cerebras engineering infrastructure.

You will work on Python frameworks, orchestration systems, distributed execution, scheduling, test infrastructure, and developer tooling. You will help define the architecture and APIs that other engineering teams depend on every day.

This role is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys reading unfamiliar code, understanding how systems fit together, debugging difficult problems, and improving the underlying design rather than applying one-off fixes.

We value strong software-engineering fundamentals, independent problem solving, and sound systems thinking more than familiarity with any particular infrastructure product.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, develop, test, and maintain Python frameworks and services used to orchestrate engineering workflows across machines and clusters.

 - Build reusable abstractions for scheduling, distributed execution, resource management, test execution, workflow planning, and failure recovery.

 - Define clear APIs, module boundaries, extension points, and data models that allow infrastructure systems to evolve without becoming difficult to maintain.

 - Reason about concurrency, asynchronous execution, multiprocessing, state management, retries, idempotency, cancellation, and partial failures.

 - Debug complex issues spanning Python applications, operating systems, processes, filesystems, networking, remote machines, and distributed services.

 - Write high-quality automated tests and documentation for infrastructure that is expected to be reliable and widely reused.

 - Partner with platform, CI, release, quality, ML systems, and product engineering teams to understand requirements and translate them into scalable software designs.

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

 - 5+ years of professional software-engineering experience.

 - Strong proficiency in Python and a solid understanding of the language’s strengths, limitations, and runtime behavior.

 - Experience designing maintainable software systems, libraries, frameworks, backend services, or developer-facing APIs.

 - Good judgment around software architecture, abstraction boundaries, design patterns, extensibility, and long-term maintainability.

 - Understanding of concurrency concepts such as processes, threads, asynchronous execution, synchronization, and shared state.

 - Foundational understanding of operating systems, including processes, signals, filesystems, resource management, and program execution.

 - Foundational understanding of distributed-systems concepts such as retries, timeouts, idempotency, partial failure, coordination, and eventual consistency.

 - Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including the ability to form hypotheses, gather evidence, and work through unfamiliar systems independently.

PREFERRED SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with Python concurrency technologies such as asyncio, multiprocessing, concurrent futures, or event-driven systems.

 - Experience building orchestration engines, workflow systems, schedulers, distributed job runners, or control-plane software.

 - Experience developing test infrastructure or extensions for frameworks such as pytest.

 - Familiarity with CI systems, build systems, release infrastructure, or developer-productivity tooling.

 - Experience with Kubernetes, containerized environments, cluster schedulers, or remote execution systems.

 - BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
